_source.dataset: Natural Earth 110m admin 0 countries, carrying how much of a twenty-four hour day the national movement guidance of five countries covers, alongside the dietary guidance each country publishes
_source.publisher: Natural Earth for the geometry, Tom Patterson and Nathaniel Vaughn Kelso. Each guidance sentence is credited to its own issuing body in countries[].documents[].publisher.
_source.licence: Public domain for the geometry. Guidance sentences are short verbatim quotations from public health pages, used for study and credited to the publisher and page they came from.
_source.period: Natural Earth 5.2.0-pre; guidance pages as published and retrieved on 2026-09-17
_source.how_these_numbers_were_made: Coordinates are longitude and latitude on an equirectangular projection: longitude -180 to 180 maps linearly to x 0 to 960, latitude 84 to -60 maps linearly to y 0 to 384. Antarctica is dropped. Every ring is decimated by keeping a point only once it has moved at least 3 units (1.2 for the five named countries), then rounded to one decimal place, then discarded if its bounding box is under 6 square units (0.8 for the five). 15 context countries fell below that and are not drawn. The categories are not derived from the geometry: each is read off one sentence of one document, quoted verbatim under the country with the URL it was read from, and every URL was checked for a 200 response on 2026-09-17 using a browser user agent.
_source.classification_note: category records how much of the twenty-four hours one national movement document covers, not how strong, how recent or how good the advice is. A country is classified from the sentence marked classifies: true and from nothing else. Where a country has no clean equivalent of NHMRC, that is recorded in gap as an absence rather than filled with a near miss.

categories.label: The whole day, every age
categories.description: Activity, sitting and sleep set together in one document, for every age band the guidance covers.

categories.label: The whole day, children only
categories.description: An integrated document covers children. The adult guidance keeps activity and sitting and drops sleep.

categories.label: The waking hours only
categories.description: Activity and sitting are recommendations. Sleep appears among the benefits claimed, never among the targets set.

countries.name: Australia
countries.summary: Did not rebuild Canada's format so much as take it, and now publishes activity, sitting and sleep as one document for every age band.

documents.publisher: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing
documents.title: 24-hour movement guidelines for all Australians
documents.quote: Australia’s 24-hour movement guidelines outline how much physical activity you should do, the importance of reducing the time you spend sitting or lying down, and how much sleep people should get.

documents.publisher: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing
documents.title: Australian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines for Adults (18-64 years) and Older Adults (65+ years): Guideline Development Report
documents.quote: The potential benefit for Australia was that it could leverage the considerable work done in Canada on the development of their 24-hour guidelines, which would allow Australia to complete what would normally be a much longer process, in considerably less time and requiring fewer resources.

documents.publisher: National Health and Medical Research Council
documents.title: Australian dietary guidelines
documents.quote: The Australian dietary guidelines (the guidelines) provide up-to-date advice about the amount and kinds of foods that we need to eat for health and wellbeing.

documents.publisher: National Health and Medical Research Council
documents.title: Guidelines
documents.quote: National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) develops and supports high quality guidelines for clinical practice, public health, environmental health and ethics.

countries.name: Canada
countries.summary: Wrote the format. The children's guideline was the first anywhere to set targets across a whole day, and the adult one followed it.

documents.title: Canadian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines for Adults aged 18-64 years: An Integration of Physical Activity, Sedentary Behaviour, and Sleep
documents.quote: For health benefits, adults aged 18-64 years should be physically active each day, minimize sedentary behaviour, and achieve sufficient sleep.

documents.title: Canadian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines for the Children and Youth (5-17 years): An Integration of Physical Activity, Sedentary Behaviour, and Sleep
documents.quote: The Canadian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines for Children and Youth (ages 5-17 years) are the first evidence-based guidelines to address the whole day.

documents.title: Canada's food guide
documents.quote: Canada's food guide is the government of Canada's guidance on healthy eating for people in Canada aged 2 years and older.

countries.gap: Nothing found here fills NHMRC's slot. The movement guideline itself comes from a professional society rather than a health department, which is a difference in who gets to speak and not only in what is said.

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.summary: Took Canada's format for children and stopped there. Its adults get eating and activity bound into one document instead, with no sleep target in it.

documents.title: Sit Less, Move More, Sleep Well: Physical Activity Guidelines for Children and Young People
documents.quote: For school-aged children and young people (aged 5 to 17 years) high levels of physical activity, low levels of sedentary behaviour and sufficient sleep each day achieves greater health benefits.

documents.title: Sit Less, Move More, Sleep Well: where the guidelines came from
documents.quote: The 24-hour Movement Guidelines for Children and Youth was developed in Canada, © 2016. They have been adapted with permission from the Canadian Society for Exercise Physiology

documents.title: Eating and Activity Guidelines for New Zealand Adults: Updated 2020
documents.quote: The Eating and Activity Guidelines for New Zealand Adults (the Guidelines) provide evidence-based recommendations on healthy eating and physical activity for New Zealand adults.

documents.publisher: Health New Zealand Te Whatu Ora
documents.title: Eating and activity guidelines
documents.quote: These documents are an important tool for health professionals and others who provide advice on nutrition and physical activity.

countries.gap: Nothing found here fills NHMRC's slot. Health New Zealand publishes a guidance library sorted by topic rather than developing guidelines to a standard of its own.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.summary: Activity and sitting across the whole life course, with sleep named among the benefits and never among the recommendations.

documents.publisher: UK Chief Medical Officers, Department of Health and Social Care
documents.title: UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines
documents.quote: This report is a UK-wide document presenting the UK Chief Medical Officers’ physical activity guidelines for different groups, covering the volume, duration, frequency and type of physical activity required across the life course to achieve general health benefits.

documents.publisher: UK Chief Medical Officers, Department of Health and Social Care
documents.title: UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines: what is in scope
documents.quote: The report also highlights the risks of inactivity and sedentary behaviour for health.

documents.publisher: Office for Health Improvement and Disparities
documents.title: The Eatwell Guide
documents.quote: The Eatwell Guide is a policy tool used to define government recommendations on eating healthily and achieving a balanced diet.

documents.publisher: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
documents.title: About our guidance
documents.quote: We use the best available evidence to develop guidance to improve health and social care.

countries.name: United States
countries.summary: The same shape as the United Kingdom: move more, sit less, and sleep counted as something activity improves rather than something to plan.

documents.publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services
documents.title: Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition
documents.quote: This second edition of the Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans provides science-based guidance to help people ages 3 years and older improve their health through participation in regular physical activity.

documents.publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services
documents.title: Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition: Key Guidelines for Adults
documents.quote: Adults should move more and sit less throughout the day.

documents.publisher: Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion
documents.title: Dietary Guidelines for Americans
documents.quote: The Dietary Guidelines for Americans (Dietary Guidelines) provides advice on nutrition intake to meet nutrient needs, promote health, and prevent disease.

countries.gap: Nothing found here fills NHMRC's slot. Two federal departments issue the dietary guidelines together and one of them issues the activity guidelines, and no single body across health topics turned up in this reading.
